title: Access Events Archive — pipeline design, retention tiers, and runbook
content:
Purpose and scope:

This doc captures the proposed implementation notes for storing, indexing, and retaining access/audit events (we call them "access-events") produced by RBAC v2, auth flows, admin console actions, and system-level changes that are relevant for compliance (SOX/PCI/GDPR), incident investigations, and SIEM exports. Focus areas: storage layout, retention tiers, indexing strategy for search/forensics, backfill approach, failure modes and runbook steps, and integration points with evidence automation and SIEM export.

Design goals (non-exhaustive):
- Single source-of-truth object store for raw events (immutable) with fast search index for recent window (90 days).
- Cost-efficient long-term retention (1–7 years depending on policy) with clear tombstone and deletion automation.
- Deterministic backfill and reindexing process that can operate per-tenant and per-time-window.
- Auditability: every transformation must be reversible/traceable; keep raw payloads and transformation metadata.
- Minimal impact on production throughput; use async pipelines (Kafka -> processor -> S3/Index) and observable checkpoints.

Storage topology and partitioning:

Primary raw store: S3 (us-west-2 primary region)
- Bucket: s3://redwood-access-events-raw
- Object key layout: tenant_id=/<tenant_id>/year=YYYY/month=MM/day=DD/hour=HH/event_ts=<ts>_<uuid>.json.gz
- Rationale: easy date/tenant partitioning for lifecycle policies and backfills. gzip+json for simplicity; keep compression level tuned for CPU vs storage tradeoffs.

Cold/Archive: S3 Deep Archive for >365 days (per policy) or Glacier when required by customer contract. Separate prefix per customer for private-retention rules.

Indexed store: ElasticSearch (managed cluster) for hot window (90 days by default)
- Index naming: access-events-YYYY.MM.DD (roll daily), aliased per-tenant for queries (alias: access-events-tenant-<tenant>).
- Mappings: keep event fields flattened and avoid deeply nested objects to reduce ES cost. Use keyword fields for ids, date for event_ts, text+keyword for message.

Warehouse (analytics/compliance): BigQuery dataset with daily ingestion job from S3 for 90+ day aggregates and longer-term audit queries.

Event schema and versioning:

Canonical fields to capture (minimum):
- event_id (uuid)
- event_ts (ISO8601)
- tenant_id
- principal_id (user/service id)
- principal_snapshot_roles (array) -> record of RBAC v2 roles at time of event (stringified if necessary)
- principal_ip
- action (string e.g., "grant-role", "model-deploy", "api-request")
- resource_type
- resource_id
- outcome (success|failure|unauthorized)
- request_payload (raw, redacted per policy)
- response_summary
- ingest_meta: {source, producer_version, schema_version, transform_id}  <-- store as flattened fields: ingest_source, producer_version, schema_version, transform_id

Schema versioning:
- Every producer stamps schema_version (v1, v2, ...). Transformation processors must retain original_schema_version and add index_schema_version. Backfill jobs will translate from original -> index schema using documented transforms stored alongside the job.

Evidence automation tie-ins:
- Every event that is evidence-worthy (policy: outcome=unauthorized OR action in [policy-change, data-export, key-rotation]) must have an evidence pointer created by evidence automation service. Pointer fields: evidence_id, evidence_bucket_prefix, evidence_status. Evidence automation will copy the raw object and any correlated artifacts (console screenshots, session recordings) to s3://redwood-evidence/<tenant>/... and create a canonical manifest.
- Evidence retention may override global retention; flagged evidence must be retained according to legal holds. Use DynamoDB table legal-holds to control deletion for prefixes.

Pipeline implementation (high-level):
- Producers -> Kafka topic: access-events.v1 (partitioned by tenant_hash)
- Consumer group: transform-workers (k8s autoscaled) -> validate & enrich (RBAC role snapshot lookup from Vault/graph DB), redact PII per tenant policy -> write raw event to S3 (atomically) -> emit indexing message to indexing-topic
- Indexer -> batch windowed writes to ES (bulk API) and also run small streaming writes for critical events.
- Daily job reconciler: compactor that ensures S3 objects and ES docs are consistent (compare counts/hashes for windows).

Backfill strategy and guarantees:
- Use S3 as source-of-truth. Backfill job (batch backfiller) reads raw objects for a given time window and tenant, applies transforms (from versioned transform library), and writes to ES and warehouse. Backfill idempotency: mark processed objects in a sidecar DynamoDB or write marker object s3://.../backfill/processed/<tenant>/<date>/<event_id>.marker to avoid double-processing.
- For large backfills (months), use parallel workers partitioned by hour ranges to reduce time to complete. Throttle to avoid ES overload.

Failure modes and mitigations (operational notes):
- Consumer crash after S3 write but before indexing message emitted: reconcilier picks up S3-only objects and enqueues them to reindex-topic. Ensure S3 write is atomic and contains ingest_meta.transform_id to correlate.
- ES bulk failures (mapping conflict / document too large): move failing doc to dead-letter S3 prefix with error metadata; alert on high DLQ rates and enqueue manual reprocessing job that can apply schema fixes or field truncation.
- Kafka retention pressure: if producers backpressure, have fallback direct-to-S3 path (edge-case) and alert.
- Cross-region replication lag (for DR): replicate raw S3 prefixes asynchronously; if replication fails, audit fails to notify. Add DR monitors on replication metrics.

Monitoring and alerts (SLOs):
- Ingest latency P95 < 10s from producer publish to S3 write.
- Indexing latency P95 < 30s for critical events, <5m for bulk events.
- Daily reconciliation mismatch rate <0.01%.
- DLQ rate threshold -> pager.

Runbook (quick):
1) Missing events in ES for a tenant/day: run s3-list for prefix tenant/year/month/day and count objects; run backfill job with that prefix. If large, run hourly parallel backfill.
2) High DLQ volume: tail s3://.../dlq/<date>, inspect first 10 examples, classify (schema vs size vs permission). If mapping conflict, open quick PR to mapping and run small reindex for affected docs.
3) Evidence pointer failed to create: check evidence-service logs, ensure IAM role for evidence copier can read raw object. Manual: copy object to evidence prefix and mark evidence_id in DynamoDB.
4) ES cluster CPU/heap alerts: set read-only on hot indices, scale ES nodes, prioritize indexing-critical events by routing to separate high-priority index.

Security notes (KMS / access control):
- Raw S3 objects encrypted with KMS CMK. Use separate CMKs for evidence vs raw events. Key rotation must be logged and not break decryption for archived data.
- IAM roles: producer principals get PutObject to their tenant prefix only. Transform workers use role with read on raw bucket and PutObject on indexable bucket and evidence prefix.
- RBAC v2 snapshots: store role names/ids only; avoid storing expanded permissions if possible to reduce PII/exposure.

Retention automation and deletion policy: 
- Default policy: 90 days hot (ES), 1 year standard S3, 7 years archive for regulated tenants. 
- Deletion flow: 1) Mark candidate objects with delete_markers prefix and add legal-hold check -> 2) Lifecycle rule triggers move to archive/Glacier -> 3) After hold expiry run a purge job that checks manifests & writes an immutable audit record of deletion (delete_audit_log table).
- For GDPR erasure: replace raw object with redacted tombstone object (retain metadata needed for audit but strip PII) and record erasure action in delete_audit_log.

Testing and QA:
- Synthetic event generator per tenant to exercise full pipeline and failure injection (network, ES errors).
- Backfill dry-run mode: simulate transform and emit statistics without writing to ES, produce checksum report.
- Runbook drills quarterly: restore-from-archive, backfill for 1-week window, evidence retrieval test.

Outstanding questions / TODOs:
- Decide canonical place for principal_snapshot_roles: store array vs compressed JSON string. Tradeoff: queryability vs index cost.
- Finalize per-tenant retention tiers and contract fields to drive automation.
- Define cost model for ES index retention vs BigQuery for long-term searchable retention.
- Legal: confirm required retention durations per region/customer.

Appendix quick links:
- transforms library: github.com/redwood-inference/transforms#access-events
- evidence service runbook: confluence:SEC-4702
- SIEM export spec: confluence:SEC-4811

Notes: this is a working doc — expect to iterate. Main immediate action: align retention tiers with legal and product (next 2 weeks), spike backfill performance for a 90-day -> 2-year reindex (target: finish within 24h for a mid-sized tenant).
